task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.description: Review the submitted account, vehicle and party details, damage photos, police report reference, and any repair estimate for presence and usability. Identify missing or unclear items and determine whether the available materials appear sufficient for initial adjuster handling, distinguishing items needed now from an estimate that may be pending.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: this check occurs once per claim and typically involves one pass through a small set of submitted items; an incomplete or unclear item adds some review but is not assumed to require obtaining it. The resulting effort is moderate relative to the later policy and incident evaluations.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Compare the claim with policy and available records
operational_subtasks.description: Compare the reported loss date, insured, vehicle, and loss circumstances with the applicable policy and available administrative claim records. Identify apparent mismatches or potential coverage questions for the adjuster without making a final coverage decision.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: a basic policy and available-record check occurs once per claim; about 15–25% may require an additional interpretation pass for an apparent discrepancy or coverage question. The lookup and comparison make this somewhat more effortful than checking submitted-material completeness.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Evaluate incident evidence for specialist-routing indicators
operational_subtasks.description: Review the reported collision account, damage photos, and available police or incident records for reported injuries, conflicting accounts, indicators of possible fraud, or other signs that the circumstances require specialist attention. Identify the relevant evidence or uncertainty without deciding liability.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: this review occurs once per claim; roughly 15–30% may require closer comparison of conflicting or otherwise concerning details. Reviewing several evidence types together makes the typical effort moderate to high, while the estimate does not include resolving the underlying questions.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Determine readiness and route the claim
operational_subtasks.description: Using the completeness, policy, and incident reviews, determine whether the claim can enter the usual claims process or needs specialist attention, and whether missing information should be flagged for the receiving team. Send the claim to the appropriate claims team or adjuster with a concise handoff identifying readiness, missing documents or information, and any coverage or incident concerns; leave final coverage and liability decisions to the adjuster.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Assumption: one routing and handoff occurs per claim, with about 20–35% routed to a specialist; preparing a concise summary and selecting the receiving team is a relatively brief activity after the reviews are complete. Specialist routing may require slightly more tailoring, but no separate investigation or follow-up is included.
